comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C45-C51 regarding functional validation of crosslinked substrate. Both evaluations support that AAC-DNPT retains ATPase activity and can undergo IF to OF transitions. OpenEval emphasizes this as critical evidence for the experimental approach, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the substrate stimulates ATP hydrolysis.

Both address MD simulation claims C94-C102. OpenEval finds the simulations strongly support structural observations with unbiased progression and agreement with cryoEM data. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about physiological relevance, noting the simulations are based on covalently-trapped structures and questioning whether TM1 conformations reflect native conditions.

Both address QZ-Ala characterization (C30-C34). OpenEval provides detailed support for efflux ratio data demonstrating Pgp-mediated transport. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these foundational data as background for AAC-DNPT design without raising concerns.

Both address crosslinking approach and mutant generation (C35-C43). OpenEval supports the differential crosslinking behavior and ATP-dependent crosslinking at position 971. Peer reviewers unanimously praise the crosslinking methodology, with all three reviewers explicitly acknowledging the innovative approach and calling findings convincing.

Both address IF structures (C52-C61). OpenEval supports the high-resolution structures and substrate densities, noting resolutions of 3.8-4.3 Å are adequate. Peer reviewers unanimously support structural findings, with editor stating authors determined structures in 'previously unforeseen outward-facing conformations' and calling them convincing.

Both address OF structures (C62-C70). OpenEval emphasizes excellent resolutions (2.6-3.1 Å) and multi-model analysis capturing conformational heterogeneity. Peer reviewers support structural findings as convincing, with Reviewer 1 noting these are the first substrate-bound conformations of Pgp.

Both address substrate coordination patterns (C82-C83). OpenEval supports observations as consistent across structures and aligned with substrate hydrophobic nature. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these coordination details as part of overall structural findings they describe as convincing.

Both address G72A functional validation (C103-C107). OpenEval supports the mutant data showing reduced drug resistance and impaired ATPase stimulation with statistical significance. Peer reviewers implicitly accept functional validation, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging crosslinked substrates stimulate ATP hydrolysis.

Both address G72A structural characterization (C108-C113). OpenEval supports structural explanation for functional defects, noting heterogeneity and missing helices suggest inability to accommodate substrate. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this interpretation as part of overall convincing findings.

Both address TM1 regulatory role (C86-C93). OpenEval supports progressive TM1 changes correlating with substrate position as strong evidence for regulatory function. Peer reviewers explicitly support TM1 mechanism, with Reviewer 1 describing it as a 'new mechanistic model' and editor calling findings 'mechanistically important.'

Both address substrate translocation pathway (C71-C76). OpenEval supports convergence of ligand positions as strong evidence for single export pathway contradicting dual-pathway models. Peer reviewers support TM1 mechanism and note 'novel insights in the translocation pathway,' though do not specifically address single vs. dual pathway debate.

Both address late-stage intermediate and substrate entry direction (C77-C81). OpenEval supports structural measurements and inferences about translocation. Peer reviewers support overall TM1 mechanism findings but do not specifically address these intermediate state details.

Both address divergence from bacterial transporters (C120-C121) and overall mechanism synthesis. OpenEval supports the mechanism with appropriate caution about divergence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about physiological relevance and generalizability, with Reviewer 1 questioning if TM1 conformations reflect native conditions and Reviewer 3 noting limitation of single substrate.

Both address main findings summary including crosslinking strategy (C6-C7). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from structural, computational, and functional data. Peer reviewers unanimously praise crosslinking approach with all three reviewers explicitly acknowledging innovation and calling findings convincing.

Both address TM1 regulatory role and alternative exit mechanism (C8-C10). OpenEval strongly supports conclusions based on converging evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly support TM1 mechanism as novel and mechanistically important, though express some uncertainty about physiological relevance.
Both address G72 importance (C11). OpenEval supports functional validation ruling out folding issues. Peer reviewers implicitly accept G72 data as part of convincing overall findings.

Both address alternative exit mechanism diverging from established models (C12-C13). OpenEval strongly supports conclusions. Peer reviewers acknowledge novel proposal but express reservations about physiological relevance and generalizability, with concerns about covalent trapping and single substrate limitation.

Both address broader impact and significance (C126). OpenEval supports work's comprehensive validation. Peer reviewers explicitly support broader impact, with Reviewer 3 stating model will stimulate new experiments and editor noting potential for rational drug design.

OpenEval addresses double-ligand structure hypothesis (C122-C124) with uncertain evaluation, noting speculation requires more validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific hypothesis about functional significance of double-ligand binding.

Peer reviewers implicitly accept QZ-Ala characterization (C30-C34) as foundational background data. While OpenEval R1 addresses overlapping claims, peer R8 specifically focuses on these parent compound claims without corresponding dedicated OpenEval result.

Peer reviewers accept substrate coordination details (C82-C83) as part of overall structural findings. While OpenEval R8 addresses these claims along with tunnel closure (C84-C85), peer R9 specifically focuses only on coordination without corresponding evaluation of tunnel closure claims.
